newsitem.title: UK: British forces launch security operation in Belfast.
newsitem.headline: British forces launch security operation in Belfast.

text.p: British forces in Northern Ireland launched a security clampdown in an Irish nationalist stronghold in Belfast on Saturday after making overnight arrests.
Soldiers and police sealed off a house in the Whiterock area in the west of the city but declined to say if guerrilla weapons had been found.
Police said that a security operation that started when they were called to a house late on Friday was still underway but declined to give further details.
"A number of persons were taken into custody," a spokesman said. Residents said at least five people had been arrested at the house.
The city's Irish News newspaper said local people had complained about "heavy-handedness" by the security forces.

It reported that police and soldiers had mounted several large-scale raids for arms in the run-up to Christmas. Three weeks ago they uncovered a haul of suspected IRA guerrilla morars, incendiary devices and ammunition.

The operation comes at a time of heightened tension after attacks by Irish Republican Army guerrillas opposed to British rule, and fears that a two-year-old ceasefire by pro-British Loyalist foes may be over.
